items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in serial cardiology clinic notes (most recently 2026-05-28). Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin only - no oral anticoagulant order is active. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age >=75, type 2 diabetes, prior stroke/TIA with residual deficits, coronary/atherosclerotic vascular disease, female sex); guideline-recommended anticoagulation is absent. Aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a current order (2026-07-29 to 2027-01-05), a QT watch-list drug. The most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT about 515 ms and QTc (Bazett) about 523 ms, >=500 ms, requiring prescriber review per the QT monitoring memo. QTc rose from about 413 ms on the preceding ECG (108780865, 2025-06-07) after amiodarone was started in November 2025. Most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (2026-04-20) are normal.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (first appearance in the clinic medication list). The start falls between 9/1/2025 and 2/28/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12. Because the start precedes 3/1/2026 the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies, so an ECG was due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, within the window; requirement met.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02. As the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded at the 2026-03-07 visit, within the window; requirement met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10, so under the revised 3/1/2026 memo an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was recorded 2026-04-29 - five days after the deadline - so the monitoring requirement was not completed within the required time and is overdue as of the evaluation date.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was newly started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG after 2025-12-25 exists in the chart (most recent tracing 106035722, 2025-12-25, predates the start), so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. The nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no ECG for this patient exists in the chart. The outside tracing could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15. Under the revised 3/1/2026 memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since the start (most recent tracing 104253928, 2025-03-09), but the deadline falls after the 2026-09-24 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr Kessler documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted 2026-09-05, four days after the change, so the monitoring requirement was completed.

On 2026-09-10 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (authorised to adjust warfarin under the standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. Per the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 on 2026-08-22, before the change; no INR has been drawn since, so the required follow-up INR is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded diagnosis, restated in every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28). Only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant order is active and none appears in any clinic medication list. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery as vascular disease), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended. The remote coded 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' is a historical peri-procedural event, not a documented ongoing contraindication.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis. Current clinic medication list (2026-07-10) is carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine - no anticoagulant order is active. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female sex). Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention; no documented contraindication (thrombocytopenia is coded historically but no current platelet-based decision is documented).

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-prescribed at the 2026-08-20 cardiology visit (order active to 2026-12-28) even though outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. That review is not documented, so the anticoagulant is continuing against an outstanding hold for a major bleed; he is also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further raising bleeding risk.

Two direct oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was never stopped and it is still listed among current medications in that same note. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban confers a high bleeding risk, particularly with CLL and on furosemide.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 records 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded the same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular rhythm with no discernible P waves and RR intervals ranging 348-720 ms, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of about 139-144 bpm. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the discrepancy needs reconciliation because it affects rate control and anticoagulation decisions.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a current order (2026-04-23 to 2027-01-02) and escitalopram is on the clinic QT watch list. The most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT about 478 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 509 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, which per the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo requires prescriber review. Most recent electrolytes are normal (K 4.1 mEq/L, Mg 2.1 mg/dL on 2025-08-23), so the prolongation is not explained by electrolyte depletion. The ECG is nearly three years old and a repeat tracing is advisable.

Citalopram 40 mg daily is a current order (2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25) and citalopram is on the clinic QT watch list. The most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT about 488 ms and QTc (Bazett) about 528 ms, above the 500 ms threshold that requires prescriber review. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal. The 40 mg daily dose also exceeds the citalopram dose limit recommended because of QT prolongation.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a current order (2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05) and amiodarone is on the clinic QT watch list. The most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT about 532 ms and QTc (Bazett) about 521 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold. Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (2026-02-14) are within range. This 95-year-old woman is also on metoprolol, so bradycardia plus QT prolongation on amiodarone warrants prescriber review and a current tracing.

interpretations.explanation: 2026-03-07: sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with upright P waves in II/aVF and negative in aVR, PR 174 ms, narrow QRS 80 ms, QTc (Bazett) 372 ms, frontal axis about +36 degrees, no bundle branch block. Only tracing on file, so no comparison possible. Consistent with the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm; no QT concern despite citalopram.

2025-07-15: sinus rhythm at 104 bpm, regular (RR 572-584 ms), PR about 120 ms, QRS 98 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 434 ms, axis about +35 degrees, no bundle branch block. There is marked ST-segment deviation (ST elevation in V1-V2, depression laterally) with a large R wave, but conduction intervals are normal. Compared with 100698634 (2025-06-20, sinus tachycardia 147 bpm, QRS 98 ms, QTc about 425 ms): rate slower, no new AF/flutter, no block change and QTc change under 60 ms.

2024-05-21: sinus tachycardia at 110 bpm, regular, PR about 110 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 428 ms, axis about +47 degrees. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison.

2026-06-10 19:36: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - irregularly irregular RR intervals (348-650 ms, RMSSD 98 ms, 55 percent of successive differences >50 ms) and no discernible P waves, only fibrillatory baseline activity. Mean ventricular rate about 144 bpm. QRS 102 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 431 ms, axis about +6 degrees, no bundle branch block; PR not measurable. Compared with 107914094 earlier the same day (17:13, also atrial fibrillation at about 139 bpm, QTc about 431 ms) there is no change. This contradicts the same-day note describing normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm.

2025-08-02: sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, regular, PR 142 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 432 ms, frontal axis about -26 degrees (borderline leftward but within normal limits). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 104232242 (2025-04-27, sinus rhythm 60 bpm, QTc about 405 ms, apparent limb-lead reversal with negative lead I): rhythm unchanged, no block change and QTc change under 60 ms.

2024-05-23: sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular (RR 608-620 ms), PR about 105 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 379 ms, axis about -3 degrees. No bundle branch block, no AV block. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison.

2025-12-25: sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular, PR 132 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 408 ms, axis about +20 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison. This tracing predates the 2026-08-01 start of escitalopram and therefore cannot serve as the post-start ECG.

2024-11-15: atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response - irregularly irregular RR intervals (696-1164 ms, RMSSD 287 ms) and absent P waves. Mean ventricular rate about 53 bpm. QRS 88 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 383 ms, axis about +24 degrees, no bundle branch block; PR not measurable. Compared with 107873952 (2024-11-12, sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves, PR 158 ms, QTc about 385 ms) this represents NEW_AF; QTc is unchanged.

2025-03-09: sinus rhythm/mild sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with slight sinus arrhythmia, PR about 112 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 397 ms, axis about +60 degrees, no bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 106045460 (2025-03-08, sinus 62 bpm, QTc about 440 ms): no rhythm or conduction change; QTc difference about 43 ms, below the 60 ms threshold. This ECG predates the 2026-09-15 haloperidol start.
2025-08-23: sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, regular, PR 132 ms, QRS 74 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 396 ms, axis about +55 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison.

2020-06-19: sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 68 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 434 ms, axis about +57 degrees, no bundle branch block. Compared with 109048192 (2020-02-02, sinus rhythm 75 bpm with very low-amplitude, broad T waves and QTc about 512 ms) the corrected QT has shortened by roughly 78 ms, meeting QTC_DECREASE_60. No rhythm or conduction change.

2021-01-18: regular sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm (RR 494-504 ms) with a low-amplitude P wave preceding each QRS, PR about 190 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc (Bazett) 385 ms, axis about +63 degrees, no bundle branch block. Compared with 2016-09-16 (106186980, sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QRS 102 ms, QTc 387 ms): rate slightly faster but no new rhythm, conduction or QTc change (QTc difference 2 ms). Low overall voltage on both tracings.

2025-06-23: sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm with a prolonged PR interval of about 214 ms (P onset to QRS onset), i.e. first-degree AV block. Every P wave is followed by a QRS. QRS 84 ms (narrow, no bundle branch block), QTc (Bazett) about 373 ms, axis about +16 degrees. Compared with 103042067 (2024-11-30, sinus bradycardia 51 bpm, PR about 185 ms, QTc about 353 ms): no rhythm change, no bundle branch block and QTc change under 60 ms; the PR has lengthened slightly into the first-degree AV block range.

2025-09-13: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - chaotically irregular RR intervals (288-580 ms, RMSSD 104 ms) and no organised atrial activity. Mean ventricular rate about 152 bpm. QRS 100 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 403 ms, axis about -15 degrees, no bundle branch block; PR not measurable. Compared with 107374881 (2025-09-12, sinus rhythm about 77 bpm with one premature beat, QTc about 402 ms) this is NEW_AF; QTc unchanged.

2025-11-23: sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with upright P waves in II and negative P in aVR, PR about 160 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 384 ms, axis about +2 degrees, no bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 105362569 (2025-11-21, sinus rhythm 67 bpm with a long broad T wave and QTc about 524 ms) the corrected QT has shortened by about 140 ms, meeting QTC_DECREASE_60. Matches the same-day note describing sinus rhythm.

2025-02-15: sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular, PR 172 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 412 ms, axis about +66 degrees. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison.

2023-06-26: regular sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm (RR 536-540 ms) with a P wave before each QRS, PR about 155 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 391 ms, axis about +31 degrees, no bundle branch block. Very deep S wave in V1 (3.0 mV) with tall lateral R waves, consistent with left ventricular hypertrophy. Compared with 102955795 (2022-07-04, sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QRS 96 ms, QTc about 395 ms) there is no change. No atrial flutter is captured on this tracing despite the coded flutter history.

2025-03-14: sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with a single premature beat and compensatory pause (RR 936-996 ms with one 538/1372 ms couplet); the underlying rhythm is regular sinus with an upright P wave in II before each QRS, PR about 190 ms. QRS 106 ms (no bundle branch block), QTc (Bazett) about 354 ms, frontal axis about -33 degrees (left axis deviation). Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison. Importantly this tracing shows sinus rhythm, so it does not by itself exclude the documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

2026-04-29: regular rhythm at 69 bpm with a consistent atrial deflection before each QRS, PR about 132 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 375 ms. All net limb-lead QRS forces are negative in I, II and aVF with positive aVR, giving a frontal axis of about -172 degrees (extreme axis); the pattern is that of left/right arm lead reversal and the placement should be checked. No bundle branch block or AV block. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison. QTc is normal on escitalopram, but the tracing was obtained 19 days after the drug start, outside the required 14-day window.

2023-11-10: sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR about 150 ms, QRS 100 ms, axis about +43 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave is broad and late with QT about 488 ms giving QTc (Bazett) about 528 ms - marked QT prolongation. Compared with 107149156 (2020-06-17, sinus tachycardia 132 bpm, QRS 96 ms, QTc about 432 ms) the QTc has risen by roughly 95 ms, meeting QTC_INCREASE_60. Relevant to the current citalopram 40 mg daily order.

2026-03-08: sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular, PR about 136 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 392 ms, axis about +47 degrees, no bundle branch block or AV block. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison. Obtained 24 days after the 2026-02-12 escitalopram start and satisfies the 30-day post-start ECG requirement; QTc is well below 500 ms.

2019-01-13: sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, regular, PR 158 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 349 ms, frontal axis about -14 degrees. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 108651109 (2018-12-13, sinus rhythm 66 bpm, QRS 104 ms, QTc about 382 ms): no rhythm change, no new block, QTc change about 33 ms (below threshold).

2023-10-08: sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR about 128 ms, QRS 94 ms, axis about +35 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave is broad with QT about 478 ms, giving QTc (Bazett) about 509 ms - markedly prolonged. Compared with 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 74 bpm, QTc about 357 ms) the QTc has increased by roughly 150 ms, satisfying QTC_INCREASE_60. This is the tracing that triggers QT review on escitalopram.

2022-07-13: regular sinus tachycardia at 141 bpm (RR 404-454 ms, RMSSD 11 ms) with a low-amplitude but consistent P wave upright in II/III/aVF before each QRS, PR about 110 ms. QRS 82 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 417 ms, axis about -7 degrees, no bundle branch block. Compared with 109839112 (2022-07-11, atrial fibrillation with irregularly irregular RR 380-822 ms and absent P waves, rate about 110 bpm, QTc about 423 ms) organised atrial activity has returned: RESOLVED_AF. QTc essentially unchanged.

2025-05-12: sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular, with an upright P wave in II and negative deflection in aVR before each QRS, PR about 120 ms. QRS 102 ms (upper normal, no bundle branch block pattern), QTc (Bazett) about 422 ms, axis about +30 degrees. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison.

2022-07-16: sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular, PR 160 ms, QRS 80 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 407 ms, frontal axis about -50 degrees (left axis deviation). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 102616671 (2021-05-16, sinus rhythm 87 bpm, PR about 130 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc about 389 ms, axis about +22 degrees): rhythm and conduction unchanged and QTc difference under 60 ms; the axis has shifted leftward.

2024-07-17: sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with occasional premature beats. PR is prolonged at about 208 ms (first-degree AV block). QRS is broad at 132 ms with a monophasic tall R wave in I, aVL and V6, no septal q waves and a QS/deep S complex in V1-V2 - left bundle branch block. QTc (Bazett) about 430 ms; frontal axis about -25 degrees (within normal limits but leftward, with lead II nearly isoelectric). Compared with 103686933 (2024-06-03, sinus rhythm 68 bpm, PR about 206 ms, QRS 132 ms with the same LBBB pattern, QTc about 429 ms) nothing has changed - the LBBB and first-degree AV block are pre-existing.

2025-03-19: sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, regular, PR about 136 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 417 ms, axis about +43 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Essentially unchanged from 101016166 (2025-03-18, sinus tachycardia 102 bpm, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 421 ms).

2025-09-22: sinus rhythm at 66 bpm, regular, PR 148 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 383 ms, frontal axis about -29 degrees (borderline leftward, within the normal range). No bundle branch block or AV block; QRS voltage is low in V6. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison.

2022-04-27: sinus rhythm/mild sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with organised P waves and PR about 176 ms, QRS 90 ms, axis about +33 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT is long at about 532 ms with QTc (Bazett) about 521 ms. Compared with 100867733 (2022-04-06, atrial fibrillation with rapid, chaotically irregular response - RR 324-1060 ms, rate about 131 bpm, no P waves, QTc about 428 ms): organised sinus activity has returned (RESOLVED_AF) and the corrected QT has increased by about 93 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60), consistent with amiodarone therapy.

2022-05-01: sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, regular, PR about 150 ms, QRS 72 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 405 ms, axis about +43 degrees, no bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 107274479 (2019-07-27, sinus rhythm 75 bpm, QRS 70 ms, QTc about 413 ms): rate faster but no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

2024-04-19: sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 492-500 ms), PR about 116 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc (Bazett) 408 ms, axis about +70 degrees, no bundle branch block or AV block. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison.

2021-08-23 10:07: sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101 bpm, PR 138 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc (Bazett) 404 ms, axis about +53 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Essentially identical to the tracing taken 34 seconds earlier (102910502: 100 bpm, PR 130 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 406 ms); no interval change of 60 ms or more and no rhythm or block change.

2024-10-24: sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular, PR 158 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc (Bazett) 401 ms, axis about +34 degrees, no bundle branch block; prominent left ventricular voltage (V6 R wave 3.3 mV). Compared with 104629882 (2023-05-22, sinus bradycardia 58 bpm with a single premature beat and compensatory pause, QTc about 380 ms): no rhythm change, no new block, QTc change only about 20 ms. Notably sinus rhythm - no atrial fibrillation captured on this tracing despite the AF diagnosis.

2024-12-05 14:38: regular narrow-complex sinus tachycardia at 122 bpm, PR about 120 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc (Bazett) 412 ms. Net QRS forces are negative in I, II and aVF with positive aVR, giving a frontal axis of about -177 degrees (extreme/indeterminate axis; limb-lead placement should be verified). Compared with the same-day earlier tracing 106516875 (01:33, rate 100 bpm, QRS 152 ms with an rSR' pattern and tall terminal R in V1 - right bundle branch block): the QRS has narrowed to 94 ms with loss of the terminal V1 R wave, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK. QTc fell from about 460 to 412 ms (less than 60 ms).

2025-11-24: sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, PR 160 ms, QRS 100 ms, axis about +65 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT is markedly prolonged at about 515 ms giving QTc (Bazett) about 523 ms. Compared with 108780865 (2025-06-07, sinus bradycardia 47 bpm, QTc about 413 ms) the QTc has increased by roughly 110 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60), temporally associated with starting amiodarone. Sinus rhythm is maintained - no atrial fibrillation on this tracing.

2024-09-17: atrial fibrillation - irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 386-1070 ms, RMSSD 250 ms) with no organised P waves before the QRS complexes. Mean ventricular rate about 99 bpm. QRS 82 ms (narrow), QTc (Bazett) about 407 ms, frontal axis about -62 degrees (left axis deviation). No measurable PR interval because there is no consistent atrial activity. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02. As the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded at the 2026-03-07 visit, within the window; requirement met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10, so under the revised 3/1/2026 memo an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 on 2026-08-22, before the change; no INR has been drawn since, so the required follow-up INR is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded diagnosis, restated in every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28). Only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant order is active and none appears in any clinic medication list. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery as vascular disease), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended. The remote coded 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' is a historical peri-procedural event, not a documented ongoing contraindication.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis. Current clinic medication list (2026-07-10) is carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine - no anticoagulant order is active. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female sex). Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention; no documented contraindication (thrombocytopenia is coded historically but no current platelet-based decision is documented).

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-prescribed at the 2026-08-20 cardiology visit (order active to 2026-12-28) even though outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. That review is not documented, so the anticoagulant is continuing against an outstanding hold for a major bleed; he is also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further raising bleeding risk.

Two direct oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was never stopped and it is still listed among current medications in that same note. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban confers a high bleeding risk, particularly with CLL and on furosemide.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 records 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded the same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular rhythm with no discernible P waves and RR intervals ranging 348-720 ms, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of about 139-144 bpm. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the discrepancy needs reconciliation because it affects rate control and anticoagulation decisions.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a current order (2026-04-23 to 2027-01-02) and escitalopram is on the clinic QT watch list. The most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT about 478 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 509 ms, i.e. >=500 ms, which per the 2025-01-15 QT monitoring memo requires prescriber review. Most recent electrolytes are normal (K 4.1 mEq/L, Mg 2.1 mg/dL on 2025-08-23), so the prolongation is not explained by electrolyte depletion. The ECG is nearly three years old and a repeat tracing is advisable.

Citalopram 40 mg daily is a current order (2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25) and citalopram is on the clinic QT watch list. The most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT about 488 ms and QTc (Bazett) about 528 ms, above the 500 ms threshold that requires prescriber review. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal. The 40 mg daily dose also exceeds the citalopram dose limit recommended because of QT prolongation.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a current order (2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05) and amiodarone is on the clinic QT watch list. The most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT about 532 ms and QTc (Bazett) about 521 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold. Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (2026-02-14) are within range. This 95-year-old woman is also on metoprolol, so bradycardia plus QT prolongation on amiodarone warrants prescriber review and a current tracing.

interpretations.explanation: 2026-03-07: sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with upright P waves in II/aVF and negative in aVR, PR 174 ms, narrow QRS 80 ms, QTc (Bazett) 372 ms, frontal axis about +36 degrees, no bundle branch block. Only tracing on file, so no comparison possible. Consistent with the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm; no QT concern despite citalopram.

2025-07-15: sinus rhythm at 104 bpm, regular (RR 572-584 ms), PR about 120 ms, QRS 98 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 434 ms, axis about +35 degrees, no bundle branch block. There is marked ST-segment deviation (ST elevation in V1-V2, depression laterally) with a large R wave, but conduction intervals are normal. Compared with 100698634 (2025-06-20, sinus tachycardia 147 bpm, QRS 98 ms, QTc about 425 ms): rate slower, no new AF/flutter, no block change and QTc change under 60 ms.

2024-05-21: sinus tachycardia at 110 bpm, regular, PR about 110 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 428 ms, axis about +47 degrees. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison.

2026-06-10 19:36: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - irregularly irregular RR intervals (348-650 ms, RMSSD 98 ms, 55 percent of successive differences >50 ms) and no discernible P waves, only fibrillatory baseline activity. Mean ventricular rate about 144 bpm. QRS 102 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 431 ms, axis about +6 degrees, no bundle branch block; PR not measurable. Compared with 107914094 earlier the same day (17:13, also atrial fibrillation at about 139 bpm, QTc about 431 ms) there is no change. This contradicts the same-day note describing normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm.

2025-08-02: sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, regular, PR 142 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 432 ms, frontal axis about -26 degrees (borderline leftward but within normal limits). No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 104232242 (2025-04-27, sinus rhythm 60 bpm, QTc about 405 ms, apparent limb-lead reversal with negative lead I): rhythm unchanged, no block change and QTc change under 60 ms.

2024-05-23: sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular (RR 608-620 ms), PR about 105 ms, QRS 76 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 379 ms, axis about -3 degrees. No bundle branch block, no AV block. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison.

2025-12-25: sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular, PR 132 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 408 ms, axis about +20 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison. This tracing predates the 2026-08-01 start of escitalopram and therefore cannot serve as the post-start ECG.

2024-11-15: atrial fibrillation with a slow ventricular response - irregularly irregular RR intervals (696-1164 ms, RMSSD 287 ms) and absent P waves. Mean ventricular rate about 53 bpm. QRS 88 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 383 ms, axis about +24 degrees, no bundle branch block; PR not measurable. Compared with 107873952 (2024-11-12, sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves, PR 158 ms, QTc about 385 ms) this represents NEW_AF; QTc is unchanged.

2025-03-09: sinus rhythm/mild sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with slight sinus arrhythmia, PR about 112 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 397 ms, axis about +60 degrees, no bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 106045460 (2025-03-08, sinus 62 bpm, QTc about 440 ms): no rhythm or conduction change; QTc difference about 43 ms, below the 60 ms threshold. This ECG predates the 2026-09-15 haloperidol start.
2025-08-23: sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, regular, PR 132 ms, QRS 74 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 396 ms, axis about +55 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison.

2020-06-19: sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 68 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 434 ms, axis about +57 degrees, no bundle branch block. Compared with 109048192 (2020-02-02, sinus rhythm 75 bpm with very low-amplitude, broad T waves and QTc about 512 ms) the corrected QT has shortened by roughly 78 ms, meeting QTC_DECREASE_60. No rhythm or conduction change.

2021-01-18: regular sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm (RR 494-504 ms) with a low-amplitude P wave preceding each QRS, PR about 190 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc (Bazett) 385 ms, axis about +63 degrees, no bundle branch block. Compared with 2016-09-16 (106186980, sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QRS 102 ms, QTc 387 ms): rate slightly faster but no new rhythm, conduction or QTc change (QTc difference 2 ms). Low overall voltage on both tracings.

2025-06-23: sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm with a prolonged PR interval of about 214 ms (P onset to QRS onset), i.e. first-degree AV block. Every P wave is followed by a QRS. QRS 84 ms (narrow, no bundle branch block), QTc (Bazett) about 373 ms, axis about +16 degrees. Compared with 103042067 (2024-11-30, sinus bradycardia 51 bpm, PR about 185 ms, QTc about 353 ms): no rhythm change, no bundle branch block and QTc change under 60 ms; the PR has lengthened slightly into the first-degree AV block range.

2025-09-13: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response - chaotically irregular RR intervals (288-580 ms, RMSSD 104 ms) and no organised atrial activity. Mean ventricular rate about 152 bpm. QRS 100 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 403 ms, axis about -15 degrees, no bundle branch block; PR not measurable. Compared with 107374881 (2025-09-12, sinus rhythm about 77 bpm with one premature beat, QTc about 402 ms) this is NEW_AF; QTc unchanged.

2025-11-23: sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with upright P waves in II and negative P in aVR, PR about 160 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 384 ms, axis about +2 degrees, no bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with 105362569 (2025-11-21, sinus rhythm 67 bpm with a long broad T wave and QTc about 524 ms) the corrected QT has shortened by about 140 ms, meeting QTC_DECREASE_60. Matches the same-day note describing sinus rhythm.

2025-02-15: sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular, PR 172 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 412 ms, axis about +66 degrees. No bundle branch block and no AV block. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison.

2023-10-08: sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR about 128 ms, QRS 94 ms, axis about +35 degrees, no bundle branch block. The T wave is broad with QT about 478 ms, giving QTc (Bazett) about 509 ms - markedly prolonged. Compared with 100065910 (2022-11-23, sinus 74 bpm, QTc about 357 ms) the QTc has increased by roughly 150 ms, satisfying QTC_INCREASE_60. This is the tracing that triggers QT review on escitalopram.

2024-04-19: sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 492-500 ms), PR about 116 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc (Bazett) 408 ms, axis about +70 degrees, no bundle branch block or AV block. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison.

2021-08-23 10:07: sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101 bpm, PR 138 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc (Bazett) 404 ms, axis about +53 degrees, no conduction abnormality. Essentially identical to the tracing taken 34 seconds earlier (102910502: 100 bpm, PR 130 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 406 ms); no interval change of 60 ms or more and no rhythm or block change.

2024-10-24: sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular, PR 158 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc (Bazett) 401 ms, axis about +34 degrees, no bundle branch block; prominent left ventricular voltage (V6 R wave 3.3 mV). Compared with 104629882 (2023-05-22, sinus bradycardia 58 bpm with a single premature beat and compensatory pause, QTc about 380 ms): no rhythm change, no new block, QTc change only about 20 ms. Notably sinus rhythm - no atrial fibrillation captured on this tracing despite the AF diagnosis.

2024-12-05 14:38: regular narrow-complex sinus tachycardia at 122 bpm, PR about 120 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc (Bazett) 412 ms. Net QRS forces are negative in I, II and aVF with positive aVR, giving a frontal axis of about -177 degrees (extreme/indeterminate axis; limb-lead placement should be verified). Compared with the same-day earlier tracing 106516875 (01:33, rate 100 bpm, QRS 152 ms with an rSR' pattern and tall terminal R in V1 - right bundle branch block): the QRS has narrowed to 94 ms with loss of the terminal V1 R wave, so RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK. QTc fell from about 460 to 412 ms (less than 60 ms).

2025-11-24: sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, PR 160 ms, QRS 100 ms, axis about +65 degrees, no bundle branch block. QT is markedly prolonged at about 515 ms giving QTc (Bazett) about 523 ms. Compared with 108780865 (2025-06-07, sinus bradycardia 47 bpm, QTc about 413 ms) the QTc has increased by roughly 110 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60), temporally associated with starting amiodarone. Sinus rhythm is maintained - no atrial fibrillation on this tracing.

2024-09-17: atrial fibrillation - irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 386-1070 ms, RMSSD 250 ms) with no organised P waves before the QRS complexes. Mean ventricular rate about 99 bpm. QRS 82 ms (narrow), QTc (Bazett) about 407 ms, frontal axis about -62 degrees (left axis deviation). No measurable PR interval because there is no consistent atrial activity. Single tracing on file, so no prior comparison.

arguments.explanation: 2023-06-26: regular sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm (RR 536-540 ms) with a P wave before each QRS, PR about 155 ms, QRS 94 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 391 ms, axis about +31 degrees, no bundle branch block. Very deep S wave in V1 (3.0 mV) with tall lateral R waves, consistent with left ventricular hypertrophy. Compared with 102955795 (2022-07-04, sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QRS 96 ms, QTc about 395 ms) there is no change. No atrial flutter is captured on this tracing despite the coded flutter history.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in serial cardiology clinic notes (most recently 2026-05-28). Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin only - no oral anticoagulant order is active. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age >=75, type 2 diabetes, prior stroke/TIA with residual deficits, coronary/atherosclerotic vascular disease, female sex); guideline-recommended anticoagulation is absent. Aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily is a current order (2026-07-29 to 2027-01-05), a QT watch-list drug. The most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT about 515 ms and QTc (Bazett) about 523 ms, >=500 ms, requiring prescriber review per the QT monitoring memo. QTc rose from about 413 ms on the preceding ECG (108780865, 2025-06-07) after amiodarone was started in November 2025. Most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (2026-04-20) are normal.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (first appearance in the clinic medication list). The start falls between 9/1/2025 and 2/28/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12. Because the start precedes 3/1/2026 the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies, so an ECG was due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, within the window; requirement met.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02. As the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded at the 2026-03-07 visit, within the window; requirement met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10, so under the revised 3/1/2026 memo an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was newly started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG after 2025-12-25 exists in the chart (most recent tracing 106035722, 2025-12-25, predates the start), so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG has been obtained since the start (most recent tracing 104253928, 2025-03-09), but the deadline falls after the 2026-09-24 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due.

Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted 2026-09-05, four days after the change, so the monitoring requirement was completed.

On 2026-09-10 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (authorised to adjust warfarin under the standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. Per the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 on 2026-08-22, before the change; no INR has been drawn since, so the required follow-up INR is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded diagnosis, restated in every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28). Only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant order is active and none appears in any clinic medication list. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery as vascular disease), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended. The remote coded 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' is a historical peri-procedural event, not a documented ongoing contraindication.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis. Current clinic medication list (2026-07-10) is carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine - no anticoagulant order is active. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female sex). Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention; no documented contraindication (thrombocytopenia is coded historically but no current platelet-based decision is documented).

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-prescribed at the 2026-08-20 cardiology visit (order active to 2026-12-28) even though outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. That review is not documented, so the anticoagulant is continuing against an outstanding hold for a major bleed; he is also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further raising bleeding risk.

Two direct oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was never stopped and it is still listed among current medications in that same note. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban confers a high bleeding risk, particularly with CLL and on furosemide.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 records 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded the same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular rhythm with no discernible P waves and RR intervals ranging 348-720 ms, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of about 139-144 bpm. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the discrepancy needs reconciliation because it affects rate control and anticoagulation decisions.

The ECG is nearly three years old and a repeat tracing is advisable.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10, so under the revised 3/1/2026 memo an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was newly started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG after 2025-12-25 exists in the chart (most recent tracing 106035722, 2025-12-25, predates the start), so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted 2026-09-05, four days after the change, so the monitoring requirement was completed.

Per the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 on 2026-08-22, before the change; no INR has been drawn since, so the required follow-up INR is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded diagnosis, restated in every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28). Only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant order is active and none appears in any clinic medication list. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery as vascular disease), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended. The remote coded 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' is a historical peri-procedural event, not a documented ongoing contraindication.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis. Current clinic medication list (2026-07-10) is carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine - no anticoagulant order is active. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female sex). Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention; no documented contraindication (thrombocytopenia is coded historically but no current platelet-based decision is documented).

That review is not documented, so the anticoagulant is continuing against an outstanding hold for a major bleed; he is also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further raising bleeding risk.

Two direct oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was never stopped and it is still listed among current medications in that same note. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban confers a high bleeding risk, particularly with CLL and on furosemide.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 records 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded the same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular rhythm with no discernible P waves and RR intervals ranging 348-720 ms, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of about 139-144 bpm. Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin only - no oral anticoagulant order is active. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age >=75, type 2 diabetes, prior stroke/TIA with residual deficits, coronary/atherosclerotic vascular disease, female sex); guideline-recommended anticoagulation is absent. Aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF.

The most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT about 515 ms and QTc (Bazett) about 523 ms, >=500 ms, requiring prescriber review per the QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (2026-04-20) are normal.

ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10, so under the revised 3/1/2026 memo an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-04-24. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 on 2026-08-22, before the change; no INR has been drawn since, so the required follow-up INR is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded diagnosis, restated in every cardiology clinic note through 2026-07-28). Only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant order is active and none appears in any clinic medication list. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery as vascular disease), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended. The remote coded 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' is a historical peri-procedural event, not a documented ongoing contraindication.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and prior cardioembolic cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis. Current clinic medication list (2026-07-10) is carvedilol, metoprolol tartrate and famotidine - no anticoagulant order is active. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female sex). Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for secondary stroke prevention; no documented contraindication (thrombocytopenia is coded historically but no current platelet-based decision is documented).

That review is not documented, so the anticoagulant is continuing against an outstanding hold for a major bleed; he is also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further raising bleeding risk.

The 2026-07-15 note states the intent was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but rivaroxaban was never stopped and it is still listed among current medications in that same note. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban confers a high bleeding risk, particularly with CLL and on furosemide.

Both ECGs recorded the same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular rhythm with no discernible P waves and RR intervals ranging 348-720 ms, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of about 139-144 bpm.
